text: Press them on a signal and transmit the signal to the receiver. In parallel, and the receiver will be able to receive them at the same time but independently. So we have multiple outputs. So if you use them at the transmitter and the receiver, this means that if using only one pair of antennas, you could transmit, for example, at one megabit per second. Using four of them, you can now transmit at four megabits per second in total, right? Because each is considered as an independent transmission. Therefore, if you have four antennas here, four multiple inputs, right, and four outputs, four antennas at the receiver, you can transmit in parallel for strings of bits, let's say, instead of one. So you can increase your data rate by a factor of four. So that's why in the more recent versions of the physical layer Wi-Fi, we said we are using OFDM plus MIMO. So we are using OFDM, that's a way to increase the data rate possible data rate. But we are also further increasing the data rate by deploying more antennas at the transmitter and more antennas.
